5200: from the base of ὑετός; wet (as if with rain), i.e. (by implication) sappy (fresh):--green.
5201: from ὕδωρ; a water-jar, i.e. receptacle for family supply:--water-pot.
5202: from a compound of ὕδωρ and a derivative of πίνω; to be a water-drinker, i.e. to abstain from vinous beverages:--drink water.
5203: from a compound of ὕδωρ and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι (as if looking watery); to be "dropsical":--have the dropsy.
5204: from the base of ὑετός; water (as if rainy) literally or figuratively:--water.
5205: from a primary (to rain); rain, especially a shower:--rain.
5206: from a presumed compound of υἱός and a derivative of τίθημι; the placing as a son, i.e. adoption (figuratively, Christian sonship in respect to God):--adoption (of children, of sons).
5207: apparently a primary word; a "son" (sometimes of animals), used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship:--child, foal, son.
5208: perhaps akin to ξύλον; a forest, i.e. (by implication) fuel:--matter.
5209: accusative case of ὑμεῖς; you (as the objective of a verb or preposition):--ye, you (+ -ward), your (+ own).
5210: irregular plural of σύ; you (as subjective of verb):--ye (yourselves), you.
5211: from (the god of weddings); "hymenæal"; Hymenæus, an opponent of Christianity:--Hymenæus.
5212: from ὑμεῖς; yours, i.e. pertaining to you:--your (own).
5213: irregular dative case of ὑμεῖς; to (with or by) you:--ye, you, your(-selves).
5214: from ὕμνος; to hymn, i.e. sing a religious ode; by implication, to celebrate (God) in song:--sing a hymn (praise unto).
5215: apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of (to celebrate; probably akin to ᾄδω; compare עֲבוֹט); a "hymn" or religious ode (one of the Psalms):--hymn.
5216: genitive case of ὑμεῖς; of (from or concerning) you:--ye, you, your (own, -selves).
5217: from ὑπό and ἄγω; to lead (oneself) under, i.e. withdraw or retire (as if sinking out of sight), literally or figuratively:--depart, get hence, go (a-)way.
5218: from ὑπακούω; attentive hearkening, i.e. (by implication) compliance or submission:--obedience, (make) obedient, obey(-ing).
5219: from ὑπό and ἀκούω; to hear under (as a subordinate), i.e. to listen attentively; by implication, to heed or conform to a command or authority:--hearken, be obedient to, obey.
5220: from ὑπό and ἀνήρ; in subjection under a man, i.e. a married woman:--which hath an husband.
5221: from ὑπό and a derivative of ἀντί; to go opposite (meet) under (quietly), i.e. to encounter, fall in with:--(go to) meet.
5222: from ὑπαντάω; an encounter or concurrence (with εἰς for infinitive, in order to fall in with):--meeting.
5223: from ὑπάρχω; existency or proprietorship, i.e. (concretely) property, wealth:--goods, substance.
5224: neuter plural of present participle active of ὑπάρχω as noun; things extant or in hand, i.e. property or possessions:--goods, that which one has, things which (one) possesseth, substance, that hast.
5225: from ὑπό and ἄρχομαι; to begin under (quietly), i.e. come into existence (be present or at hand); expletively, to exist (as copula or subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as an auxiliary to a principal (verb):--after, behave, live.
5226: from ὑπό and (to yield, be "weak"); to surrender:--submit self.
5227: from ὑπό and ἐναντίος; under (covertly) contrary to, i.e. opposed or (as noun) an opponent:--adversary, against.
5228: a primary preposition; "over", i.e. (with the genitive case) of place, above, beyond, across, or causal, for the sake of, instead, regarding; with the accusative case superior to, more than:--(+ exceeding, abundantly) above, in (on) behalf of, beyond, by, + very chiefest, concerning, exceeding (above, -ly), for, + very highly, more (than), of, over, on the part of, for sake of, in stead, than, to(-ward), very. In the comparative, it retains many of the above applications.
5229: middle voice from ὑπέρ and αἴρω; to raise oneself over, i.e. (figuratively) to become haughty:--exalt self, be exalted above measure.
5230: from ὑπέρ and the base of ἀκμήν; beyond the "acme", i.e. figuratively (of a daughter) past the bloom (prime) of youth:--+ pass the flower of (her) age.
5231: from ὑπέρ and ἄνω; above upward, i.e. greatly higher (in place or rank):--far above, over.
5232: from ὑπέρ and αὐξάνω; to increase above ordinary degree:--grow exceedingly.
5233: from ὑπέρ and the base of βάσις; to transcend, i.e. (figuratively) to overreach:--go beyond.
5234: adverb from present participle active of ὑπερβάλλω; excessively:--beyond measure.
5235: from ὑπέρ and βάλλω; to throw beyod the usual mark, i.e. (figuratively) to surpass (only active participle supereminent):--exceeding, excel, pass.
5236: from ὑπερβάλλω; a throwing beyond others, i.e. (figuratively) supereminence; adverbially (with εἰς or κατά) pre- eminently:--abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure.
5237: from ὑπέρ and εἴδω; to overlook, i.e. not punish:--wink at.
5238: from ὑπέρ and the neuter plural of ἐκεῖνος; above those parts, i.e. still farther:--beyond.
5239: from ὑπέρ and ἐκτείνω; to extend inordinately:--stretch beyond.
5240: from ὑπέρ and the alternate form of ἐκχέω; to pour out over, i.e. (passively) to overflow:--run over.
5241: from ὑπέρ and ἐντυγχάνω; to intercede in behalf of:--make intercession for.
5242: from ὑπέρ and ἔχω; to hold oneself above, i.e. (figuratively) to excel; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) superior, superiority:--better, excellency, higher, pass, supreme.
5244: from ὑπέρ and φαίνω; appearing above others (conspicuous), i.e. (figuratively) haughty:--proud.
5245: from ὑπέρ and νικάω; to vanquish beyond, i.e. gain a decisive victory:--more than conquer.
5246: from ὑπέρ and ὄγκος; bulging over, i.e. (figuratively) insolent:--great swelling.
5247: from ὑπερέχω; prominence, i.e. (figuratively) superiority (in rank or character):--authority, excellency.
5248: from ὑπέρ and περισσεύω; to super-abound:--abound much more, exceeding.
5249: from ὑπέρ and περισσῶς; superabundantly, i.e. exceedingly:--beyond measure.
5250: from ὑπέρ and πλεονάζω; to superabound:--be exceeding abundant.
5251: from ὑπέρ and ὑψόω; to elevate above others, i.e. raise to the highest position:--highly exalt.
5252: from ὑπέρ and φρονέω; to esteem oneself overmuch, i.e. be vain or arrogant:--think more highly.
5253: neuter of a derivative of ὑπέρ; a higher part of the house, i.e. apartment in the third story:--upper chamber (room).
5254: from ὑπό and ἔχω; to hold oneself under, i.e. endure with patience:--suffer.
5255: from ὑπακούω; attentively listening, i.e. (by implication) submissive:--obedient.
5256: from ὑπηρέτης; to be a subordinate, i.e. (by implication) subserve:--minister (unto), serve.
5257: from ὑπό and a derivative of (to row); an under-oarsman, i.e. (generally) subordinate (assistant, sexton, constable):--minister, officer, servant.
5258: from an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to ὑπό through the idea of subsilience); sleep, i.e. (figuratively) spiritual torpor:--sleep.
5259: a primary preposition; under, i.e. (with the genitive case) of place (beneath), or with verbs (the agency or means, through); (with the accusative case) of place (whither (underneath) or where (below) or time (when (at)):--among, by, from, in, of, under, with. In the comparative, it retains the same general applications, especially of inferior position or condition, and specially, covertly or moderately.
5260: from ὑπό and βάλλω; to throw in stealthily, i.e. introduce by collusion:--suborn.
5261: from a compound of ὑπό and γράφω; an underwriting, i.e. copy for imitation (figuratively):--example.
5262: from ὑποδείκνυμι; an exhibit for imitation or warning (figuratively, specimen, adumbration):--en-(ex-)ample, pattern.
5263: from ὑπό and δεικνύω; to exhibit under the eyes, i.e. (figuratively) to exemplify (instruct, admonish):--show, (fore-)warn.
5264: from ὑπό and δέχομαι; to admit under one's roof, i.e. entertain hospitably:--receive.
5265: from ὑπό and δέω; to bind under one's feet, i.e. put on shoes or sandals:--bind on, (be) shod.
5266: from ὑποδέω; something bound under the feet, i.e. a shoe or sandal:--shoe.
5267: from ὑπό and δίκη; under sentence, i.e. (by implication) condemned:--guilty.
5268: neuter of a compound of ὑπό and ζυγός; an animal under the yoke (draught-beast), i.e. (specially), a donkey:--ass.
5269: from ὑπό and ζώννυμι; to gird under, i.e. frap (a vessel with cables across the keel, sides and deck):--undergirt.
5270: from ὑπό and κάτω; down under, i.e. beneath:--under.
5271: middle voice from ὑπό and κρίνω; to decide (speak or act) under a false part, i.e. (figuratively) dissemble (pretend):--feign.
5272: from ὑποκρίνομαι; acting under a feigned part, i.e. (figuratively) deceit ("hypocrisy"):--condemnation, dissimulation, hypocrisy.
5273: from ὑποκρίνομαι; an actor under an assumed character (stage-player), i.e. (figuratively) a dissembler ("hypocrite":--hypocrite.
5274: from ὑπό and λαμβάνω; to take from below, i.e. carry upward; figuratively, to take up, i.e. continue a discourse or topic; mentally, to assume (presume):--answer, receive, suppose.
5275: from ὑποτρέχω and λείπω; to leave under (behind), i.e. (passively) to remain (survive):--be left.
5276: neuter of a presumed compound of ὑπό and ληνός; vessel or receptacle under the press, i.e. lower wine-vat:--winefat.
5277: a prolonged form for ὑπολείπω; to leave behind, i.e. bequeath:--leave.
5278: from ὑπό and μένω; to stay under (behind), i.e. remain; figuratively, to undergo, i.e. bear (trials), have fortitude, persevere:--abide, endure, (take) patient(-ly), suffer, tarry behind.
5279: from ὑπό and μιμνήσκω; to remind quietly, i.e. suggest to the (middle voice, one's own) memory:--put in mind, remember, bring to (put in) remembrance.
5280: from ὑπομιμνήσκω; a reminding or (reflexively) recollection:--remembrance.
5281: from ὑπομένω; cheerful (or hopeful) endurance, constancy:--enduring, patience, patient continuance (waiting).
5282: from ὑπό and νοιέω; to think under (privately), i.e. to surmise or conjecture:--think, suppose, deem.
5284: from ὑπό and πλέω; to sail under the lee of:--sail under.
5285: from ὑπό and πνέω; to breathe gently, i.e. breeze:--blow softly.
5286: neuter of a compound of ὑπό and πούς; something under the feet, i.e. a foot-rest (figuratively):--footstool.
5287: from a compound of ὑπό and ἵστημι; a setting under (support), i.e. (figuratively) concretely, essence, or abstractly, assurance (objectively or subjectively):--confidence, confident, person, substance.
5288: from ὑπό and στέλλω; to withhold under (out of sight), i.e. (reflexively) to cower or shrink, (figuratively) to conceal (reserve):--draw (keep) back, shun, withdraw.
5289: from ὑποστέλλω; shrinkage (timidity), i.e. (by implication) apostasy:--draw back.
5290: from ὑπό and στρέφω; to turn under (behind), i.e. to return (literally or figuratively):--come again, return (again, back again), turn back (again).
5291: from ὑπό and στρώννυμι; to strew underneath (the feet as a carpet):--spread.
5293: from ὑπό and τάσσω; to subordinate; reflexively, to obey:--be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto.
5294: from ὑπό and τίθημι; to place underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to hazard, (reflexively) to suggest:--lay down, put in remembrance.
5295: from ὑπό and τρέχω (including its alternate); to run under, i.e. (specially), to sail past:--run under.
5296: from a compound of ὑπό and a derivative of τύπος; typification under (after), i.e. (concretely) a sketch (figuratively) for imitation:--form, pattern.
5297: from ὑπό and φέρω; to bear from underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to undergo hardship:--bear, endure.
5298: from ὑπό and χωρέω; to vacate down, i.e. retire quietly:--go aside, withdraw self.
5299: from a compound of ὑπό and a derivative of ὀπτάνομαι; to hit under the eye (buffet or disable an antagonist as a pugilist), i.e. (figuratively) to tease or annoy (into compliance), subdue (one's passions):--keep under, weary.
